title: Drawings & Release
description: Drawing content, process-specific notes, assembly drawings and BOMs, revision control, checking and supplier release packages.

items.text: Part number in the title block matches the PDM/PLM record and the file name
items.hint: Compare the title block, model properties and PDM record. Mismatches cause wrong parts to be quoted, ordered or built.

items.text: Revision letter in the title block matches the latest entry in the revision table
items.hint: A title block that disagrees with the revision table makes the revision ambiguous at the supplier.

items.text: Material is specified fully, with grade, standard or manufacturer and trade name
items.hint: "Aluminum" or "ABS" is not a specification. Give alloy and temper, or resin grade and supplier, plus any approved equivalents.

items.text: Finish is specified (anodize type and color, plating, paint, texture) or stated as none
items.hint: Reference the finish spec or Materials & Finishes callout. A blank finish field is often read as "as machined" or "as molded".

items.text: Units are stated on the drawing (mm by default) and used consistently
items.hint: Dual dimensions, if any, show the primary unit clearly. Mixed units on one sheet are a recipe for scrap.

items.text: Projection angle (first or third angle) is stated with the standard symbol
items.hint: Suppliers in different regions default to different projection angles. A missing symbol can mirror a view interpretation.

items.text: Drawing scale is stated and views not at the sheet scale are labeled with their own scale
items.hint: Detail and section views often use a different scale. Remind readers not to scale the drawing.

items.text: Sheet number and total sheet count are shown on every sheet
items.hint: "Sheet 2 of 3" lets a supplier know a page is missing from the package.

items.text: Drawn, checked and approved fields carry names and dates
items.hint: An empty checked field means the drawing was not independently checked. Match the names to the PDM approval record.

items.text: The general tolerance note or title-block tolerance table is present and matches the chosen tolerance standard
items.hint: Confirm the note references the general tolerance standard and class selected during tolerancing (see Tolerancing & GD&T). Leftover template tolerance blocks are a frequent error.

items.text: Applicable drawing and GD&T standards are stated (e.g. ASME Y14.5 edition or ISO GPS)
items.hint: The standard sets how every symbol is interpreted. Use the company template field rather than a free note so it is never omitted.

items.text: Part mass or weight is shown where the drawing template calls for it
items.hint: Use the CAD mass with the correct material density applied. Mass is useful for incoming checks and for BOM rollups.

items.text: The drawing has enough views to define every feature without ambiguity
items.hint: Check that hidden or internal features appear in at least one view where they can be dimensioned. A feature shown only in an isometric is undefined.

items.text: Section and detail views are provided for internal geometry, small features and complex profiles
items.hint: Section through bosses, ribs, grooves and undercuts. Label section lines and views consistently.

items.text: Every feature is fully defined by dimensions, GD&T or a reference to the 3D model
items.hint: Review each feature in turn and confirm its size and location are controlled. Missing dimensions get filled in by the supplier's guess.

items.text: No dimension is duplicated across views or sheets
items.hint: Duplicates diverge after the next revision. Use the CAD tool's duplicate dimension check where available, then scan by eye.

items.text: Dimensions originate from datum features rather than chaining from edge to edge
items.hint: Chained dimensions accumulate tolerance. Baseline or ordinate dimensioning from the datum frame matches how the part is inspected.

items.text: Reference dimensions are marked as reference and are not used to control features
items.hint: Use parentheses or REF per the stated standard. An unmarked redundant dimension creates a conflict.

items.text: Dimensions are driven from the model and not overridden with manually typed values
items.hint: Search for overridden or detached dimensions in the CAD drawing. A typed value that disagrees with the model is a silent error.

items.text: When the 3D model is the master definition, the drawing states this and identifies the governing model and revision
items.hint: Model-based definition (e.g. per ASME Y14.41) needs a note naming the model file, revision and what the drawing still controls. Otherwise the supplier cannot tell which governs when they disagree.

items.text: Features controlled only by the model are identified and given a general profile tolerance
items.hint: A note such as "all untoleranced surfaces profile X to datums A|B|C per model" closes the gap. Without it, model-only geometry has no tolerance.

items.text: Text, dimensions and symbols are legible at the printed sheet size and do not overlap geometry
items.hint: Print or view at 100% on the intended sheet size. Overlapping dimensions are misread.

items.text: Threads, holes and countersinks use standard hole callouts rather than manual notes
items.hint: Use the CAD hole callout so depth, thread class and countersink angle stay linked to the feature.

items.text: Edge break and deburr requirements are stated (e.g. per ISO 13715 or a general edge note)
items.hint: Sharp edges cut assemblers and users; uncontrolled breaks affect seals and fits. State exceptions where sharp edges are functional.

items.text: Surface finish (Ra) is specified on functional surfaces and as a general value elsewhere
items.hint: Call out Ra on sealing faces, bearing bores and sliding surfaces using the stated standard's symbol. Leave non-functional surfaces to the general note to avoid cost.

items.text: Heat treatment, hardness and case depth are specified where required, with the test method
items.hint: Give the hardness scale and location of measurement. State whether dimensions apply before or after heat treatment.

items.text: A cosmetic specification is referenced for customer-facing surfaces
items.hint: Reference the cosmetic spec that defines surface classes, allowable defects, viewing conditions and SPI or VDI 3400 finish where applicable.

items.text: Part marking is specified: content, location, method and size
items.hint: Include part number, revision, cavity number, date code, material ID or regulatory marks as required. Mark location must not land on a cosmetic or functional surface.

items.text: RoHS, REACH and other substance compliance requirements are stated on the drawing or in a referenced spec
items.hint: Use a standard compliance note so suppliers certify every lot. Missing notes lead to non-compliant platings and coatings.

items.text: Cleanliness, biocompatibility or particulate requirements are stated for patient- or fluid-contacting parts
items.hint: Reference the cleaning spec or ISO 10993 evaluation basis for patient-contact parts. Suppliers will not apply cleaning steps that are not specified.

items.text: Notes are numbered, current and free of template leftovers that do not apply
items.hint: Delete inherited notes that conflict with this part (wrong material, wrong process). Flag-note symbols on the views should match the note numbers.

items.text: Packaging and handling requirements are stated where the part is fragile or cosmetic
items.hint: Specify protective film, separators or trays so cosmetic and precision parts arrive undamaged.

items.text: Resin is specified by manufacturer, grade and color code, with any approved alternates
items.hint: Name the resin grade and color masterbatch or pre-color code. Generic resin names let the molder substitute.

items.text: Surface texture or polish is specified by standard (SPI, VDI 3400 or texture supplier code) for each surface
items.hint: Show texture zones on a view and give the code per zone. Texture affects draft, so confirm draft supports the texture.

items.text: Gate location and allowable gate vestige are shown or restricted
items.hint: Mark permitted gate zones and maximum vestige height. Leaving it open lets the toolmaker gate on a Class A surface.

items.text: Ejector pin locations and allowable witness marks are restricted on cosmetic and functional surfaces
items.hint: Show keep-out zones for ejectors and state allowable witness depth or protrusion.

items.text: Parting line location and allowable mismatch and flash are specified
items.hint: Show the parting line and state the maximum flash and step per the molder's capability. Flash on a sealing surface causes leaks.

items.text: Sink and void acceptance criteria are stated for surfaces over ribs and bosses
items.hint: Reference the cosmetic spec or give limits for sink on visible faces opposite ribs and bosses.

items.text: Cavity identification and date code inserts are specified on the drawing
items.hint: Cavity ID lets quality trace defects to a specific cavity; date wheels support lot traceability.

items.text: A flat pattern view is included with overall blank size
items.hint: The flat pattern confirms the supplier's unfold matches yours. Note that the flat is for reference and the formed part governs, unless agreed otherwise.

items.text: Bend notes give direction, angle and inside radius for every bend
items.hint: Include bend up/down and radius in a bend table. Inside radius should match the supplier's tooling.

items.text: Material thickness, grade and grain or rolling direction (where it matters) are specified
items.hint: Grain direction affects cracking on tight bends in some alloys. State it when bends are near the material's minimum radius.

items.text: Hardware inserts (PEM-style nuts, studs, standoffs) are called out with supplier part numbers
items.hint: Give the hardware manufacturer's part number and the installation side. Generic "M3 nut" callouts get substituted.

items.text: Dimensions to formed features are given from the side that is controlled (inside or outside of bend)
items.hint: Indicate inside versus outside mold line dimensions. Ambiguity here shifts features by a material thickness.

items.text: Burr direction is specified where it affects safety, assembly or cosmetic surfaces
items.hint: Punching leaves a burr on one side. Specify burr side away from users, cables and seals.

items.text: Threads are specified with size, pitch, class and depth (e.g. M5x0.8-6H, full thread depth)
items.hint: Specify thread class per ISO 965 or the applicable standard and the minimum full-thread depth. Unspecified depth leaves the tap-drill depth to the machinist.

items.text: Thread inserts (helical coil, key-locking) are specified with manufacturer part numbers and tapped hole spec
items.hint: Give the insert part number and the insert manufacturer's tapped-hole size. The hole spec differs from a standard thread.

items.text: Internal corner radii are compatible with standard cutters or are explicitly called out
items.hint: Sharp inside corners cannot be milled. Show the maximum allowable radius so the shop can choose the tool.

items.text: Surface finishes on machined functional surfaces are specified separately from the general finish
items.hint: Call out Ra on sealing, bearing and sliding surfaces. Do not over-specify a fine general finish.

items.text: Finish masking requirements are shown for threads, bores and grounding points
items.hint: Mark areas to be masked from anodize, plating or paint. Unmasked grounding pads break electrical bonding.

items.text: Machining stock is shown on as-cast surfaces that will be machined
items.hint: Provide a casting drawing with stock allowance, or a combined drawing that distinguishes as-cast and machined dimensions.

items.text: As-cast tolerances reference a casting tolerance standard or the foundry's agreed grade
items.hint: ISO 8062 grades or a supplier-agreed table. Do not apply machining tolerances to as-cast features.

items.text: Porosity acceptance class and inspection method are specified for critical zones
items.hint: Reference the agreed radiographic or sectioning standard and zone the drawing where porosity matters (sealing faces, threads, high-stress areas).

items.text: The as-cast part and the machined part are separate, linked definitions (part numbers or drawing views)
items.hint: Foundries are quoted and inspected on the as-cast condition, machinists on the finished part. Linking both on one ambiguous view causes disputes over which dimensions the foundry owns.

items.text: Impregnation, heat treatment or stress relief requirements are stated where needed
items.hint: Vacuum impregnation seals porosity for pressure-tight castings; state it with the spec if required.

items.text: Every balloon on the assembly drawing matches an item in the BOM, and every BOM item is ballooned
items.hint: Cross-check the balloon list with the BOM table. Orphan balloons or missing items cause build errors.

items.text: BOM quantities and units of measure are correct for every line, including bulk items
items.hint: Check quantities against the model and give units for adhesives, tapes and cables (mm, g, mL). Bulk items without units cause shortages.

items.text: Purchased parts list the manufacturer and manufacturer part number
items.hint: A description alone is not orderable. Include the exact catalog number, including any variant suffixes.

items.text: Approved alternates for purchased parts are listed or explicitly forbidden
items.hint: List qualified alternates or state "no substitution". Unlisted substitutes may differ in critical dimensions or materials.

items.text: Fastener torque values are specified for every threaded joint
items.hint: Give torque in N·m with tolerance and the tool or method. Torque values should come from the joint analysis (see Assembly, Fastening & DFA).

items.text: Adhesive and thread-locker callouts give product, application area and cure requirements
items.hint: Name the product and grade, show where to apply it and state cure time or conditions before handling.

items.text: Assembly sequence notes are given where order matters
items.hint: Call out steps that cannot be reversed (adhesive, press fits, heat-staking) and any orientation requirements.

items.text: Assembly-level dimensions and checks are shown for critical interfaces
items.hint: Include the final gaps, heights or alignments the line must verify, with tolerances from the stack-ups.

items.text: Lubrication, grease or potting callouts are specified with product and quantity
items.hint: "Lubricate" without product or amount gets interpreted differently by each operator.

items.text: Label and marking placements are shown on the assembly drawing
items.hint: Show product label, serial and regulatory mark locations with orientation.

items.text: The revision table lists each revision with a description of the change
items.hint: Descriptions such as "updated" are useless. Name what changed and where (zone or view).

items.text: Each revision references its ECO/ECN number
items.hint: Traceability to the change order connects the drawing to the reason, approval and affected parts.

items.text: Model and drawing revisions match in the PDM/PLM system
items.hint: Check that the drawing references the released model revision. A drawing pointing to a work-in-progress model can carry unapproved geometry.

items.text: The drawing is released through PDM/PLM, not sent from a local or working file
items.hint: Released state locks the file and records approvals. Files emailed from a workspace bypass the release process.

items.text: Changed features are identified on the drawing (revision clouds or triangles) for the current revision
items.hint: Clouding lets suppliers and checkers find the change quickly. Clear old clouds when the next revision starts.

items.text: STEP and PDF exports are generated from the released revision and stored with it
items.hint: Regenerate exports at release rather than reusing earlier files. Check the STEP opens and the PDF revision matches.

items.text: Native CAD files are archived with the release
items.hint: Archive the native files and references (or a Pack and Go) so the design can be reproduced later.

items.text: Suppliers receive controlled copies and superseded revisions are withdrawn
items.hint: Send from PDM/PLM or a controlled portal and confirm the supplier acknowledges the new revision. Superseded copies at the supplier are a common cause of wrong parts.

items.text: Interchangeability is assessed for each revision and part number changed when form, fit or function changes
items.hint: If old and new parts are not interchangeable, the part number should change. Bumping only the revision mixes incompatible parts in stock.

items.text: Where-used is checked for every changed part so affected assemblies and drawings are updated
items.hint: Run the PDM where-used report. Shared parts often affect other products.

items.text: Each drawing is checked by someone other than the author
items.hint: An independent checker catches errors the author cannot see. Record the checker in the title block and PDM.

items.text: The drawing checklist was completed and stored with the release
items.hint: Store the completed checklist in PDM with the release so later reviews can see what was checked.

items.text: All checker redlines are closed or dispositioned before release
items.hint: Each redline is either incorporated or answered with a reason. Open redlines at release are deferred errors.

items.text: The checker compared the drawing against the model, stack-ups and CTF list
items.hint: Check that CTF dimensions carry the tolerances the stack-ups assume. The drawing and stack-up analysis are often out of sync.

items.text: A print-out or PDF review was done at final sheet size
items.hint: Errors hidden by on-screen zoom (overlapping text, missing leaders) show up on a full-size print.

items.text: The RFQ package contains drawings, 3D models, specifications and referenced documents at matching revisions
items.hint: Send one zip or portal package with a document list. Missing referenced specs (cosmetic, finish, packaging) are the usual gap.

items.text: Annual volumes, lot sizes and ramp schedule are stated in the RFQ
items.hint: Volume drives tooling choice (cavity count, soft versus hard tooling) and price. Quotes without volumes cannot be compared.

items.text: Inspection requirements and the critical dimensions list are included in the package
items.hint: State which dimensions need measurement on every lot, SPC or certificates. Suppliers quote inspection cost from this.

items.text: First article inspection (FAI) requirements are specified: quantity, report format and full-dimension scope
items.hint: State the FAI format (e.g. AS9102-style or PPAP if required), number of parts per cavity and which documents are returned.

items.text: Material certifications and compliance declarations required from the supplier are listed
items.hint: Specify mill certs, resin lot certificates, RoHS/REACH declarations and conflict-minerals statements as required.

items.text: Tooling ownership, tool life and maintenance expectations are stated for production tooling
items.hint: Agree who owns the tool, expected shot life and who pays for repair. Leaving this open causes disputes at transfer.

items.text: Supplier questions and deviations from the RFQ are logged and answered in writing
items.hint: Track supplier DFM feedback and agreed deviations, and fold accepted ones into the next drawing revision.
